D018-D011_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling on edge for maybe… eight or nine months now. It got worse after something that happened at the pharmacy last year, but I’m not even sure what’s connected to what anymore.

Sleep has been rough. I keep having these really vivid dreams where I’m back in that moment at work and I wake up with my heart racing, sometimes sweating, and it takes a while to realize I’m actually in my own bed. Sometimes it’s not the exact scene, just the same feeling of dread.

Since then, things I used to enjoy—like going out with my friends, reading fiction, even yoga—just feel flat. I go through the motions, but I don’t really care. I catch myself replaying everything and thinking, “If that doctor had listened,” or “If management had staffed us properly, this wouldn’t have happened.” I know it doesn’t change anything, but I fixate on who dropped the ball.

I still feel this kind of frozen terror when my mind goes back to it; it’s like the shock never really wore off. I’m also weirdly jumpy. If someone taps me on the shoulder at work, I practically jump out of my skin. Even small decisions—what to cook, which brand to order for the store—can paralyze me. I’ll stare at options way longer than makes sense, second-guessing everything, like any choice could be the wrong one.
D018-D011_h001.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D018-D011_h001.answer: C & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

    B. Acute Stress Disorder

    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D018-D011_h022.question:
It’s been… I don’t know, maybe several months now that I’ve felt like this. I keep getting these flashes in my head of what happened with my ex and that night everything blew up. They come out of nowhere—like I’ll be at an open house, talking to clients, and suddenly I’m right back there. I don’t want to think about it, but my mind just replays it anyway.

I can’t shake this feeling that it was my fault, like I should’ve seen things sooner or done something differently. Even when I close a big sale or get a compliment from a client, it just feels flat. Everyone says I’m doing great, but I don’t feel proud, just… empty, or like I don’t deserve it.

I’m on edge a lot. The smallest thing sets me off—my assistant making a minor mistake, my sister being late to dinner—and I’ll snap, raise my voice, say things I regret. I hate that I’m yelling, but in the moment it feels like pressure building and I can’t hold it in. I’m tense pretty much all the time, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen, but I can’t tell if it’s just stress from work, the divorce, or everything all together.
D018-D011_h022.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D018-D011_h022.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h023.question:
It’s been… I don’t know, maybe a few months that it’s felt like this, getting worse the last few weeks. I’m still working as an interpreter, but it’s getting harder to keep it together during assignments.

Sometimes, out of nowhere, I’ll just… lose where I am. It’s like the room drops away and I’m back in this old scene in my head. My body reacts like it’s happening again—my heart’s racing, I’m bracing myself—and then I kind of snap back and realize I’m in front of a client trying to sign and I’ve missed a few seconds. It’s really unsettling.

I’m on edge most of the time. My husband says I’m “set to explode.” The smallest things—like him chewing too loud or our neighbor’s music—make me snap or yell, and then I hate myself afterward. I carry this constant feeling that whatever happened back then was somehow my fault, like I should have stopped it or done something different.

What scares me is I feel weirdly distant from him and even from my family. I know I love them, but I don’t really feel it. It’s like there’s glass between us, and I’m just going through the motions.
D018-D011_h023.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D018-D011_h023.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h024.question:
I’ve been on the rescue team for a while, so I’m used to tough calls, but the last few months something’s been off. I keep getting these scenes popping into my head out of nowhere—like I’m back on certain calls, hearing the sirens, seeing faces. It’s not like I’m trying to think about it; it just crashes in and I sort of freeze for a second.

Since then I feel wound up all the time, like my body never powers down. Even at home with my wife, I’m on edge, waiting for something bad to happen. I’m checking my phone, listening for noises, just… tense. I’m anxious about work, about my family, about everything really, but I can’t always say what exactly I’m worried about.

What’s weird is, even when something goes really well—a good save, good feedback from the chief—I don’t feel proud. It’s like it just slides off me. My wife says I snap sometimes, and there’ve been a couple of times I’ve slammed a door hard enough to crack it, or thrown something across the room when I got overwhelmed. That’s not who I was before, and it’s starting to scare me.
D018-D011_h024.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D018-D011_h024.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h025.question:
I suppose this really started… maybe a year or so ago? It’s hard to pin down exactly.  

What I notice now is how my body reacts before my mind does. Sometimes it’s just a sound on the television, or the way a car backfires outside, or even a sudden draft in the house, and my heart just slams in my chest. My hands start shaking, my breathing goes shallow, and I feel like I’m right back in some terrible moment, even if I can’t always explain why that particular thing set me off.  

There’s this constant undercurrent of dread, like something awful is about to happen, even when I’m just sitting in my chair doing my crossword. I wake up some mornings already tense. I can’t seem to relax, and my thoughts immediately jump to worst‑case scenarios about my children and grandchildren.  

What bothers me most is I feel… hollow with them. I know I care, but it’s like there’s a sheet of glass between us. When they hug me, I go through the motions, but I don’t really feel it. And every so often, if I get startled or overwhelmed, I’ve slammed a door so hard it cracked, or shoved someone away more roughly than I meant to.
D018-D011_h025.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D018-D011_h025.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder
